recommendation_summary: The reply recommends adding XLOOKUP formulas to the user's existing Excel workbook, so that typing a part code returns its shelf location and price, and drops all new apps and services.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the shelf and the selling price for a part code about 40 times a day, off the paper slip. You asked which stack to build. The list is your Excel workbook, 240 unique codes, which you already update on the counter laptop. Lookups are read-only and only you do them.
labels.Deleted: Retool, Supabase, Next.js, a separate database, accounts, and hosting. Those add a second copy of the list you already edit and a service to keep running.
labels.Bottleneck: Scrolling the sheet to match a code from the slip to one of 240 rows.
labels.Checked myself: What you told me: Excel is on the counter laptop, that workbook is the list you update, the codes are unique, and every lookup happens on that machine. I have not opened the file.

note: All four labelled lines appear before the workbook lookup recommendation and each one addresses this decision; the reply names Retool, Supabase and Next.js as deleted, never offers them again, and says it has not opened the file.
